title: Mary Gay Scanlon raises concerns over Epstein investigation and constitutional values - South Delco News
text:
Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, who represents Pennsylvania’s 5th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of statements on her official X account on September 17, 2025, addressing issues related to the Jeffrey Epstein case and constitutional values.
In her first post at 19:22 UTC, Scanlon questioned ongoing efforts for accountability in the Epstein case: “Is holding the people involved with Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes accountable a misleading factor?”.
Shortly after, at 19:39 UTC, she referenced financial investigations linked to Epstein: “Banks flagged $1.5 billion in suspicious transactions relating to Epstein’s sex trafficking.
I tried to subpoena Secretary Bessent so the American people could follow the money.
Republicans voted for continuing the cover-up.”
Later that day at 20:36 UTC, Scanlon reflected on Constitution Day and civic responsibility: “Today, and every day, we celebrate the signing of our Constitution in Philadelphia, which created a democratic republic based on the rule of law, not the whims of a few or the imposition of martial law.
It’s up to all of us to continue the quest to form a more perfect union and”.
Mary Gay Scanlon has served as U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania’s 5th District since 2018 after succeeding Pat Meehan. She was born in Watertown, New York in 1959 and currently resides in Swarthmore. Scanlon earned her undergraduate degree from Colgate University in 1980 and completed her Juris Doctor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1984.
